### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b2118f49c0f5b0a4b267b327bc8cfd257f182a8`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b2118f49c0f5b0a4b267b327bc8cfd257f182a8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8a4dae2029626827918ec2f2316e0264220646e4` — the merge of head `df48c97363e1ca90bf6b33e6b6472bd89bad1209` into base `0b2118f49c0f5b0a4b267b327bc8cfd257f182a8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8a4dae2029626827918ec2f2316e0264220646e4 && git checkout 8a4dae2029626827918ec2f2316e0264220646e4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0b2118f49c0f5b0a4b267b327bc8cfd257f182a8 df48c97363e1ca90bf6b33e6b6472bd89bad1209 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0b2118f49c0f5b0a4b267b327bc8cfd257f182a8 && git merge --no-ff df48c97363e1ca90bf6b33e6b6472bd89bad1209

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b2118f49c0f5b0a4b267b327bc8cfd257f182a8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0b2118f49c0f5b0a4b267b327bc8cfd257f182a8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `21b1caaeb462395ea257ed76f095ad5080dbe27d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/discovery-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/discovery-schema-conformance.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__rest__src__discovery-routes.ts.json + read, not reviewed: docs/adr/0138-guest-model-anonymous-principal-doors-grants-and-organization.md (D2, note of 2026-11-20, on main), packages/spec/src/system/restriction-profile.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/restriction-profile.ts, packages/rest/src/openapi-builtin-paths.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-openapi-route.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-config-mount-table.pin.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/anonymous-door-sweep.classification.ts, scripts/check-dual-build-cjs-loads.mjs, .changeset/34774-restriction-profile-route.md

Read at the merge base `59392ed1d` against the head: 6 files, +172 / -32. Check-runs on the head as read (52): 28 success, 16 skipped, 8 in progress, 0 failed. In progress: Test Core 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 of 10. Completed green include Build Core, the four Type Check jobs, every Lint job, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Test Core 5/10 and 10/10. The Dogfood shard job is skipped on the PR run. This record does not vouch for the eight pending shards: the shard that runs `discovery-schema-conformance.test.ts` had not necessarily answered, and the dev's own test readings are at `9398ea17f`, not at this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set, route table: with `api.enableProjectScoping` on, `GET {basePath}/environments/:environmentId/discovery/restriction-profile` is no longer registered. Right: the only executable change is the `if (!isScoped)` guard around one `routeManager.register` call in `registerDiscoveryEndpoints`; the handler body inside is re-indented and otherwise identical, and `isScoped` is the registrar's existing reading, the one the `/discovery` handler and about twenty sibling registrars use.
- Accept-set, unscoped route: `GET {basePath}/discovery/restriction-profile` is unchanged (same handler, same empty `RESTRICTION_PROFILE_PARAMS`, same 503 arm, still inside `enableDiscovery`). Right. `scripts/check-dual-build-cjs-loads.mjs` and `rest-config-mount-table.pin.test.ts` both read the unscoped path with scoping off and are unaffected.
- `projectResolution: 'required'`: `registerRoutes` calls `registerForBase(scopedBase)` alone, so the server mounts no restriction-profile route. Right as a reading of the code, and stated in the changeset, the `registerRoutes` docblock and the registrar comment. On main such a server served the profile on the scoped path only.
- Public surface, exports: none added, removed or re-typed. `DiscoveryRouteHost` and `RESTRICTION_PROFILE_PARAMS` are untouched. The one published text that moves is the `registerRoutes` docblock, which now names the exception; it agrees with the code.
- Derived documents: the scoped base's `openapi.json` built-in section is produced from `getRoutes()`, so it loses the operation with the mount, and `/discovery` never advertised the route in `routes.*`. Both stay consistent with ADR-0076 (advertise what is mounted). Right.
- Ledger and anchor (check d): the ledger row stays the one unscoped row `GET /api/v1/discovery/restriction-profile`; its note and the file header now say it has no scoped mirror; the anchor JSON moves `each mounted once per base` to the discovery and OpenAPI documents and states the profile is on the unscoped base only. All three agree with the guard. The anchor attributes the unscoped-only fact to the card, not to ADR-0138, which is correct while the ADR text is unrevised.
- Tests: the `[#34774]` suite no longer reads the scoped path; the new `[#36198]` suite reads absence three ways (`getRoutes()`, the route manager, the host's `IHttpServer` under five verbs) with a populated-mount control, covers `auto`, `optional` and `required`, and reads 404 on the real `HonoHttpServer` router. `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` is already a dependency of `packages/rest` and already imported by sibling tests. The pins are not vacuous as written; whether they are green on this head is the pending Test Core shards' answer.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/rest` `patch` with a BREAKING banner and an ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. That matches AGENTS.md as it reads on main (lines 1025 to 1031): `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — correct against main, which is what cloud pins by commit. Against any published npm version nothing narrows: the route and its twin arrived together in f5cfdd21 (#35887, 2026-11-21), whose changeset `.changeset/34774-restriction-profile-route.md` is still unconsumed on main; `packages/rest/CHANGELOG.md` on main has 0 hits for the route and `packages/rest/package.json` is at 18.6.0. The changeset says so itself (`it has only ever been served by builds that include that change`), so the banner does not overstate. Check c: `never shipped` holds on what this clone can show. The clone is shallow: the version commit `958ee0359` the dev cites is not present here, so the ancestry reading was not reproduced; the unconsumed changeset is the evidence relied on.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question (do the three prose corrections outside the claimed surface stay): answered by the seat in card comment 7083375576, option A. Agreed on the tree: each of the three stated a both-bases mount this change makes false, one in a published docblock, and none changes behaviour.
- Dev deviation 5 (file-surface breach): closed by the same comment.
- Dev deviations 1, 2, 3 (dogfood battery, final-head tests, two gates NOT MEASURED locally): CI's to answer. `Build Core` and `Type Check · debt ledger` are green on the head, which covers deviation 3. Test Core is 2 of 10 green with 8 pending, and the dogfood shards are skipped on the PR run, so the six dogfood files that read this surface are answered only by the merge-queue run. I read `anonymous-door-sweep.classification.ts`: its `discovery` row matches the unscoped route alone and no dogfood test names a scoped restriction-profile path, so nothing there is expected to turn; that is a reading, not a run.
- Escalated to the maintainer, for notice: ruling comment 7077639745 transcribes C as binding the ADR-0138 D2 twin clause `in the same PR`. The PR carries no `docs/adr/` path; the seat moved the wording to #36086 in comment 7083375576. The PR body cites a process rule (an implementation card's surface carries no `docs/adr/` path); I did not find that rule spelled in AGENTS.md on main, which only names `docs/adr/**` as governed. Steve said 「C」; the `same PR` binding is the seat's transcription, and the seat changed it. See N1 for what the note owes.
- Cloud carrier: cloud's anonymous-surface ledger row for the twin is cloud's to drop; nothing in this repository reads it.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No query, no id materialisation, no join; the diff touches route registration only.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes a refusal real; it takes no declared capability away at the consumer.

- Check a, what the published spec declares: nothing in `packages/spec` names the route on either base. `restriction-profile.zod.ts` declares the profile's shape and that an environment publishes it, with no path. `rest-server.zod.ts` says scoping covers `data/meta/AI APIs`, that control-plane routes stay unscoped, and that `required` means the environment id must be in the URL. `discovery.zod.ts` declares `scoping` and no restriction-profile entry. No spec route ledger row and no contract test promises the scoped path. The only text that names the twin is ADR-0138 D2's note, and it admits the twin to the anonymous discovery role `where environment scoping mounts it`: a permission on a closed list of doors, conditional on the mount, not a duty to mount.
- Against the defect: on main the twin answers `openRestrictionProfile(spec)` for any `:environmentId`, with no host input, so on a host that enforces a narrower profile it publishes facts the environment does not honour. Withdrawing the mount removes the false statement; a 404 is the loud answer. This is the shape Steve ruled (C).
- Check b, consumers: the only reader in this repository is `packages/cli/src/utils/restriction-profile.ts`, which fetches `RESTRICTION_PROFILE_ROUTE` at the target's origin, the unscoped path. Zero hits for the route under `ui/`, `apps/`, `examples/`, `skills/`, `content/` and `packages/client`. Under `auto` and `optional` the CLI reads what it read before. Under `required` the CLI got a 404 on main and gets a 404 now; no consumer in this tree breaks. After this PR a `required` open runtime gives no path at all by which a client learns the profile; before, a client that knew an environment id could read the constant on the scoped path. That constant restricts nothing and is the same for every id, so what is lost is the spec version it stated, which the scoped `/discovery` document's `version` still answers anonymously.
- Attempts to break it: (1) a greedy sibling capturing the scoped path: I did not enumerate every scoped pattern; the wire pin asserts 404 on the real `HonoHttpServer` router with the full scoped route set mounted, so its green run (pending) is the answer; (2) `enableDiscovery: false`: unchanged, the guard sits inside the registrar; (3) scoping off with `projectResolution: 'required'`: the unscoped base is registered, the route is served; (4) a custom `apiPath` that itself contains `/environments/:environmentId` would lose the route, but that reading of `isScoped` is the file's and its siblings' existing convention, not new here; (5) ADR-0076 parity: the scoped OpenAPI document and `/discovery` follow the mount; (6) `a host's own route on that path still wins by mount order` in the changeset is cloud's measurement (cloud#4920), not readable from this repository, and this diff does not change the unscoped registration it depends on.
- ADR-0138 as it reads on main: the code does not contradict the rule. D2 is a closed list of anonymous doors and this change serves one fewer; every other sentence of the note (constant open profile, no query parameter, `enableDiscovery: false` unmounts it, no `ALLOW_ROUTES` row, handler never calls `enforceAuth`) stays true of the unscoped route. The note is descriptively stale after merge: a reader will expect a twin.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N1 (nit) — ADR-0138 D2's note of 2026-11-20 still names the environment-scoped twin. Follow-up on #36086, to be knocked before this merges, not after: the clause becomes `GET {basePath}/discovery/restriction-profile` alone, and a dated note states (i) ruling C on #36198, comment 7077639745, withdraws the twin; (ii) why: the handler reads no host input, so the twin answered the constant for any environment id, including on a host that enforces a narrower profile; (iii) the twin is not mounted and a request to it gets the host's ordinary not-found answer; (iv) a server that mounts the scoped base alone (`projectResolution: 'required'`) serves no restriction profile; (v) the unscoped route is unchanged; plus the status-line entry. The replacement text in dev report 7083326461 covers all five.
N2 (nit) — `packages/rest/src/openapi-builtin-paths.ts` (outside the diff) calls the scoped mirror `a second, complete registration`; it is now complete but for this one route. Internal comment, no behaviour. Left as an accepted deviation.
N3 (nit) — the `required` case is now pinned as `no restriction-profile route`, and `os validate --target URL` against such a host answers `HTTP 404 — no environment is served at this host`, a meaning written for cloud's door. Identical before and after this PR, and on the table when C was ruled, so not this PR's to fix; worth a follow-up card so the pinned shape is a tracked gap and not a silent one. The CLI docblock beside it (`The route is cloud's, not this repository's`) has been stale since #34774.

### ① Derived judgments

## 维护者速读（席位记录 · head `df48c97363`）
